descriptionAdvanced.en: Xiamen, situated on the southeastern coast of Fujian Province, is a dynamic island city celebrated for its scenic beauty and high quality of life. The city has a long-standing tradition as a gateway to the outside world, a role amplified by its proximity to Taiwan and its designation as one of China's first four Special Economic Zones in 1980. Historically known as Amoy, Xiamen became a major hub for the international tea and silk trades during the 19th century. A significant cultural highlight is the pedestrian-only Gulangyu Island, a UNESCO World Heritage site renowned for its colonial architecture and piano heritage. Modern Xiamen is characterized by clean boulevards, lush urban parks, and a thriving high-tech sector. Xiamen University is frequently cited as one of China's most beautiful campuses, contributing to the city's vibrant and youthful atmosphere. Despite rapid urbanization, Xiamen maintains a relaxed coastal charm, enhanced by refreshing sea breezes and the rich culinary traditions of Fujian province.

en: Xiamen was established as one of China's first four Special Economic Zones in 1980.
Gulangyu Island is famous for having the world's highest number of pianos per capita.
Nanputuo Temple, located near the university, dates back to the Tang Dynasty.
Xiamen is consistently ranked among the cleanest and most livable cities in China.
The city serves as a premier global hub for the stone processing and export industry.
The Hulishan Fortress houses a massive 19th-century Krupp cannon imported from Germany.
